---
title: "match.arg() rejects the empty string even when it is one of the choices"
ref: FUN-06
categories: [Functions]
impact: cryptique
extrait: 'match.arg("", choices = c("", "a"))'
attendu: "`\"\"`, since it is one of the choices offered"
versions: "All, the error message changed in R 4.2.0"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
extension <- function(ext = c("", "a")) {
  match.arg(ext)
}
extension()
extension("a")
extension("")
```
:::

Pick **R 4.1.3** in the menu, then run again: the error is the same, with a different message.

## Why

`match.arg()` compares the value it receives with the choices using `pmatch()`, which accepts word beginnings. But `pmatch()` never matches the empty string to anything. `match.arg()` concludes that the value is not allowed.

Without an argument, the function does return `""`, the first choice by default. Things break only when you pass `""` explicitly, and the message does not even list the empty string among the possible choices.

## The remedy

Do not offer the empty string as a choice: replace it with a word.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
extension <- function(ext = c("none", "a")) {
  match.arg(ext)
}
extension("none")
```
:::
